newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips end up on continued foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips end up on continued foreign buying.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip equities closed firmer on Friday, as foreign institutions executed broad-based buy programmes, dealers and analysts said.

"There have been discretionary buy programmes operating today, with the buying concentrated on the blue-chips, but with second-liners like Ho Hup and CIMA also seeing some interest," said an institutional dealer at a foreign brokerage house in Singapore.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 4.17 points to 1172.48, while the all-share EMAS index was up just 0.37 points to 336.31.
"It has been a strong week towards the end, and any pull-backs have been temporary," said Lim Soo Chong, head of research at HLG Securities.
Tenaga closed up 20 cents to 10.30 ringgit. "The Prime Minister's statements yesterday have made it a much more comfortable stock for investors to buy," said Lim.
Telekom closed up 20 to 22.50. "The stock had come down to fairly priced levels, and was consequently picked up by investors," said Lim.
Volume stood at 269 million shares traded, valued at 2,364 million ringgit. Losers nosed out gainers 286 to 258.
